query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled, low‐temperature, phase‐selective annealing treatment applied to a eutectic high‐entropy alloy (EHEA) can simultaneously increase both strength and ductility by selectively driving recrystallization in the softer fcc (or fcc + L12) lamellae while retaining the continuous hard-phase (B2 or precipitation-strengthened) network. This duplex microstructure will enhance back‐stress strengthening (improving yield strength) and promote distributed strain hardening (enhancing ductility).
generation.material_initial_state: An as‐cast eutectic high‐entropy alloy (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi2.1) having a lamellar dual-phase microstructure comprised of a ductile fcc (or fcc + L12) phase interleaved with a hard B2 (or B2 + bcc) phase.
generation.intervention: Apply a low‐temperature, phase‐selective annealing treatment designed to preferentially recrystallize the softer fcc lamellae while leaving the hard-phase network essentially unaltered.
generation.conditions: Annealing at a temperature sufficiently low to allow selective recrystallization of the fcc regions (for example, in the range of 580–700 °C, depending on the specific alloy system) for a carefully controlled time, so that the heterogeneous lamellar structure is retained without excessive coarsening or homogenization of the phases.
generation.structural_mediator: The emergence of a duplex microstructure with fine, fully recrystallized fcc grains embedded in a coherent, retained hard-phase network, leading to a high density of phase boundaries that can store dislocations and promote back‐stress effects.
generation.mechanism: Selective recrystallization refines the soft phase (increasing strength via Hall–Petch effects) while preserving the hard-phase skeleton provides continuous constraints that generate back‐stresses and enable effective strain partitioning and crack deflection. This dual mechanism yields higher yield strength without sacrificing, and even enhancing, ductility by delaying necking.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the original as-cast state (e.g., yield strength ~750 MPa and ~18% elongation), the treatment is expected to increase yield strength by roughly 15–30% and boost uniform elongation by 20–50% via improved strain hardening.
generation.baseline: The as-cast eutectic HEA with its inherent lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure, which exhibits a trade-off of moderate strength and ductility.
generation.boundary: This intervention is anticipated to be effective only in eutectic HEAs with clearly differentiated phase-specific recrystallization kinetics (such as AlCoCrFeNi2.1) and may not directly translate to alloys lacking a pronounced dual-phase lamellar structure.
generation.uncertainty: While previous works (e.g., PMC9365806 on phase-selective recrystallization and PMC6353877/PMC6687781 on inherited lamellar microstructures) support the beneficial role of heterogeneous duplex architectures, the precise annealing temperature–time window required for selective recrystallization and the resulting magnitude of the strength–ductility improvement remain to be fully established. Uncertainty also exists regarding the sensitivity of the approach to minor compositional variations.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA samples. Subject one set to the proposed low-temperature, phase-selective annealing treatment designed to selectively recrystallize the fcc lamellae while retaining the hard-phase network; process a control set using a conventional homogeneous annealing treatment. Characterize the microstructures using EBSD and TEM to confirm the formation of the duplex microstructure in the treated samples. Perform standardized tensile tests to measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation.
measurements: Grain size distribution of fcc and hard phases (via EBSD/TEM)
Volume fraction and connectivity of the hard-phase network
Tensile yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and uniform elongation
Dislocation density mapping near phase boundaries
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the phase-selectively annealed samples do not exhibit a statistically significant simultaneous increase in both yield strength and ductility compared to the control (i.e., if either strength or ductility is inferior or unchanged relative to the as-cast or homogenously annealed baseline), then the hypothesis that phase-selective annealing yields simultaneous strength and ductility improvements will be falsified.

Multiphase materials are evidently suited for tuning their mechanical properties by means of heterostructuring. Recently, the emergence of multicomponent high entropy alloys (HEAs) has opened up the massive composition space for developing alloys with novel microstructures and properties. Eutectic HEAs (EHEAs), first proposed by Lu et al., are a special class of HEAs having promising mechanical properties in the as-cast condition. In particular, the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 nano-lamellar EHEA consisting of soft L12/FCC and hard B2 phases has attracted considerable attention due to their attractive mechanical properties over a wide temperature range, and ample opportunities for further tailoring their microstructure and properties by thermo-mechanical processing (TMP),. Bhattacharjee et al. showed that heavily cryo-rolled and annealed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA develops a complex heterogeneous microstructure consisting of retained lamellar and coarse non-lamellar regions. The individual domains again consisted of multiscale architecture ranging from ultrafine recrystallized FCC grains to coarse recovered B2 grains, which resulted in simultaneous enhancement in strength and ductility. Excellent ductility is crucial not only for shaping but also for strengthening metals and alloys. The ever most widely used eutectic alloys are suffering from the limited ductility and losing competitiveness among advanced structural materials. Here we report a distinctive concept of phase-selective recrystallization to overcome this challenge for eutectic alloys by triggering the strain hardening capacity of the duplex phases completely. We manipulate the strain partitioning behavior of the two phases in a eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) to obtain the phase-selectively recrystallized microstructure with a fully recrystallized soft phase embedded in the skeleton of a hard phase. The resulting microstructure fully releases the strain hardening capacity in EHEA by eliminating the weak boundaries. Our phase-selectively recrystallized EHEA achieves a high ductility of ∼35% uniform elongation with true stress of ∼2 GPa. This concept is universal for various duplex alloys with soft and hard phases and opens new frontiers for traditional eutectic alloys as high-strength metallic materials.
